concept_summary: FortiOS uses a block-structured CLI configuration model with config/edit/set/next/end syntax. Initial setup includes hostname, management interface addressing, admin accounts, and system services. Configuration changes take effect immediately without explicit commit. The GUI and CLI share the same underlying configuration database allowing concurrent management methods.
cli_mode_context: Enter configuration blocks with 'config <section>', edit specific objects with 'edit <name>', set parameters with 'set <parameter> <value>', use 'next' to finish editing object, and 'end' to exit configuration block.
example_commands:
config system global
 set hostname FG-HQ-FW01
 set admin-sport 8443
 set timezone 04
end
config system interface
 edit port1
  set vdom root
  set mode static
  set ip 192.0.2.10 255.255.255.0
  set allowaccess ping https ssh
  set description "Management"
 next
end
config system admin
 edit admin
  set password NewAdminP@ssw0rd
 next
end

key_parameters.description: Enters configuration section (e.g., system, firewall, router)
Edits or creates named object within section
Completes current edit block and moves to next
Displays configuration (use 'show full' for all including defaults)

concept_summary: FortiOS interfaces can operate in multiple modes including static IP, DHCP, or PPPoE. Physical and logical interfaces support VLAN sub-interfaces. Each interface is assigned to a Virtual Domain (VDOM) for multi-tenancy. Interface configuration includes IP addressing, access control for management protocols, and role assignments. Interfaces can be hardware ports, VLANs, aggregates, tunnels, or loopbacks.
cli_mode_context: Configure interfaces under 'config system interface'. Edit specific interface by name. Set IP mode, address, VDOM assignment, and management access.
example_commands:
config system interface
 edit port2
  set vdom root
  set mode static
  set ip 192.0.2.1 255.255.255.252
  set allowaccess ping
  set description "WAN-Uplink"
  set role wan
 next
 edit port3
  set vdom root
  set mode static  
  set ip 198.51.100.1 255.255.255.0
  set allowaccess ping https ssh
  set description "LAN-Internal"
  set role lan
 next
 edit port4.100
  set vdom root
  set vlanid 100
  set interface port4
  set ip 203.0.113.1 255.255.255.0
  set allowaccess ping
 next
end

key_parameters.description: Sets interface to static IP addressing
Assigns IPv4 address and subnet mask
Enables management protocols (ping, https, ssh, snmp, telnet)
Defines interface role (lan, wan, dmz, undefined)
Specifies parent physical interface for VLAN

concept_summary: FortiOS handles VLANs through software switches or hardware switches depending on platform. Software switches provide Layer 2 forwarding between interfaces while hardware switches leverage ASIC capabilities. VLAN interfaces are created as sub-interfaces of physical ports or switch members. Transparent mode allows FortiGate to operate as Layer 2 device with VLAN awareness for security policies.
cli_mode_context: Create VLAN sub-interfaces under 'config system interface' or use 'config system switch-interface' for hardware switch configurations. Specify parent interface and VLAN ID.
example_commands:
config system interface
 edit vlan100
  set vdom root
  set interface port5
  set vlanid 100
  set ip 192.0.2.1 255.255.255.0
  set allowaccess ping
  set role lan
 next
 edit vlan200
  set vdom root
  set interface port5
  set vlanid 200
  set ip 198.51.100.1 255.255.255.0
  set allowaccess ping
  set role lan
 next
end
config system switch-interface
 edit lan-switch
  set vdom root
  set member port6 port7 port8
 next
end

key_parameters.description: Explicitly sets interface type to VLAN (usually auto-detected)
Creates hardware switch for bridging multiple ports
Specifies ports included in hardware switch
Enables switch port analyzer (SPAN) for traffic mirroring

concept_summary: Static routes define explicit forwarding paths with destination, gateway, interface, and optional administrative distance. FortiOS supports multiple routing tables per VDOM and allows static route prioritization. Routes can specify both outgoing interface and gateway or use blackhole/reject for traffic control. Distance values determine preference when multiple routes exist to the same destination.
cli_mode_context: Configure static routes under 'config router static'. Create new route entry with 'edit', set destination, gateway, device, and distance parameters.
example_commands:
config router static
 edit 1
  set dst 0.0.0.0 0.0.0.0
  set gateway 192.0.2.1
  set device port2
  set comment "Default route to ISP"
 next
 edit 2
  set dst 198.51.100.0 255.255.255.0
  set device port3
  set comment "Direct connected route"
 next
 edit 3
  set dst 203.0.113.0 255.255.255.0
  set gateway 192.0.2.5
  set distance 10
 next
 edit 4
  set dst 203.0.113.128 255.255.255.128
  set blackhole enable
  set comment "Blackhole route"
 next
end

key_parameters.description: Route priority for same distance (lower is preferred)

concept_summary: FortiOS implements OSPFv2 for IPv4 with area-based hierarchical design. OSPF configuration includes router ID, area definitions, and network statements matching interfaces. Authentication, route summarization, and redistribution provide flexibility. Virtual links extend backbone connectivity. OSPF integrates with firewall policies for security-aware routing.
cli_mode_context: Configure OSPF under 'config router ospf'. Define areas and networks under respective sub-configurations. Set global parameters like router-id and redistribute settings.
example_commands:
config router ospf
 set router-id 192.0.2.1
 config area
  edit 0.0.0.0
  next
  edit 0.0.0.10
  next
 end
 config network
  edit 1
   set prefix 192.0.2.0 255.255.255.0
   set area 0.0.0.0
  next
  edit 2
   set prefix 198.51.100.0 255.255.255.0
   set area 0.0.0.10
  next
 end
 config ospf-interface
  edit "port3"
   set interface port3
   set cost 10
  next
 end
 config redistribute connected
  set status enable
 end
end

key_parameters.description: Interface metric for OSPF cost calculation
Redistributes routes from other sources into OSPF

concept_summary: FortiOS supports BGP for inter-domain routing with IBGP and EBGP capabilities. BGP configuration includes AS number, router ID, neighbor definitions, and network advertisements. Route maps provide policy control for filtering and attribute manipulation. BGP integrates with security policies enabling application-aware routing decisions. Supports IPv4 and IPv6 address families.
cli_mode_context: Configure BGP under 'config router bgp'. Set AS number and router-id globally. Define neighbors under 'config neighbor'. Advertise networks under 'config network'.
example_commands:
config router bgp
 set as 65001
 set router-id 192.0.2.1
 config neighbor
  edit 198.51.100.1
   set remote-as 65002
   set description "EBGP to ISP"
  next
  edit 192.0.2.254
   set remote-as 65001
   set update-source loopback0
   set next-hop-self enable
  next
 end
 config network
  edit 1
   set prefix 192.0.2.0 255.255.255.0
  next
 end
 config redistribute connected
  set status enable
 end
end

key_parameters.description: Neighbor AS number (same for IBGP, different for EBGP)
Sets local router as next-hop for advertised routes

concept_summary: FortiOS supports RIP for small networks with simple distance-vector routing. RIP configuration includes interface participation and version settings. IS-IS support may be limited compared to dedicated routing platforms. FortiGate focuses primarily on OSPF and BGP for dynamic routing needs with security integration.
cli_mode_context: Configure RIP under 'config router rip'. Define networks and interfaces. IS-IS configuration follows similar structure if supported on platform.
example_commands:
config router rip
 config network
  edit 1
   set prefix 192.0.2.0 255.255.255.0
  next
  edit 2
   set prefix 198.51.100.0 255.255.255.0
  next
 end
 config interface
  edit port3
   set send-version 2
   set receive-version 2
  next
 end
 set redistribute connected enable
end

key_parameters.description: Defines networks to advertise in RIP

reason: IS-IS is not supported on FortiGate platforms. RIP is available but FortiOS focuses on OSPF/BGP for dynamic routing. EIGRP is Cisco proprietary and not implemented in FortiOS.

concept_summary: FortiOS uses VRRP for interface-level redundancy and HA clustering for full device redundancy. VRRP provides virtual gateway IP sharing between multiple FortiGates. HA clustering synchronizes configuration and sessions between units for active-passive or active-active operation. Heartbeat links monitor cluster health with failover on link or device failure.
cli_mode_context: Configure VRRP under interface configuration. Configure HA clustering under 'config system ha'. Set cluster mode, priority, and monitoring.
example_commands:
config system interface
 edit port3
  set vdom root
  set ip 192.0.2.2 255.255.255.0
  set allowaccess ping
  config vrrp
   edit 1
    set vrip 192.0.2.1
    set priority 110
    set start-time 3
   next
  end
 next
end
config system ha
 set group-name FG-HA-Cluster
 set mode a-p
 set password HAClusterSecret
 set hbdev port7 50
 set session-pickup enable
 set ha-mgmt-status enable
 config ha-mgmt-interface
  edit 1
   set interface port1
   set gateway 192.0.2.1
  next
 end
 set priority 200
 set override enable
end

key_parameters.description: Cluster mode (a-p for active-passive, a-a for active-active)
Allows preemption when higher priority comes online

concept_summary: FortiOS firewall policies control traffic flow between security zones based on source, destination, service, schedule, and user identity. Policies are evaluated top-down with first-match processing. Each policy specifies action (accept, deny, IPsec), logging, NAT, and security profiles (AV, IPS, web filter, application control). Policies leverage interface roles (LAN, WAN, DMZ) and address/service objects for reusability.
cli_mode_context: Configure policies under 'config firewall policy'. Create address objects under 'config firewall address' and service objects under 'config firewall service custom'. Order matters - use 'move' to reposition policies.
example_commands:
config firewall address
 edit LAN-Subnet
  set subnet 192.0.2.0 255.255.255.0
 next
end
config firewall service custom
 edit HTTPS-8443
  set tcp-portrange 8443
 next
end
config firewall policy
 edit 1
  set name "LAN-to-WAN"
  set srcintf port3
  set dstintf port2
  set srcaddr LAN-Subnet
  set dstaddr all
  set action accept
  set schedule always
  set service ALL
  set nat enable
  set logtraffic all
 next
 edit 2
  set name "Block-Telnet"
  set srcintf any
  set dstintf any
  set srcaddr all
  set dstaddr all
  set service TELNET
  set action deny
  set logtraffic all
 next
end

concept_summary: FortiOS provides multiple NAT types including source NAT, destination NAT (virtual IPs), and policy-based NAT. Source NAT can use interface IP or IP pools. Central SNAT allows NAT without firewall policy. Virtual IPs provide port forwarding and server load balancing. NAT64 and NAT46 support IPv4/IPv6 translation scenarios. NAT is typically enabled per firewall policy.
cli_mode_context: Enable NAT in firewall policy with 'set nat enable'. Configure IP pools under 'config firewall ippool'. Configure virtual IPs under 'config firewall vip' for destination NAT. Use central SNAT for policy-independent NAT.
example_commands:
config firewall ippool
 edit SNAT-Pool
  set startip 198.51.100.10
  set endip 198.51.100.20
  set comments "Public IP pool for outbound NAT"
 next
end
config firewall vip
 edit WEB-Server-VIP
  set extip 198.51.100.50
  set mappedip 192.0.2.10
  set extintf port2
  set portforward enable
  set extport 443
  set mappedport 443
 next
end
config firewall policy
 edit 10
  set srcintf port3
  set dstintf port2
  set srcaddr all
  set dstaddr all
  set action accept
  set schedule always
  set service ALL
  set nat enable
  set ippool enable
  set poolname SNAT-Pool
 next
end

key_parameters.description: Enables source NAT in firewall policy
Uses IP pool instead of interface IP
Defines pool of public IPs for source NAT
Configures virtual IP for destination NAT

concept_summary: FortiOS provides comprehensive IPsec VPN capabilities for site-to-site and remote access scenarios. Configuration includes IKE phase 1 for authentication and key exchange, phase 2 for data encryption, and firewall policies permitting VPN traffic. Route-based VPNs use tunnel interfaces while policy-based VPNs trigger on traffic match. Supports IKEv1 and IKEv2 with multiple authentication methods including PSK and certificates.
cli_mode_context: Configure phase 1 under 'config vpn ipsec phase1-interface'. Configure phase 2 under 'config vpn ipsec phase2-interface'. Create firewall policies allowing VPN traffic. For route-based VPN, add static routes via tunnel interface.
example_commands:
config vpn ipsec phase1-interface
 edit Site-B-Tunnel
  set interface port2
  set ike-version 2
  set peertype any
  set proposal aes256-sha256
  set dhgrp 14
  set remote-gw 203.0.113.1
  set psksecret MyPreSharedKey123
 next
end
config vpn ipsec phase2-interface
 edit Site-B-P2
  set phase1name Site-B-Tunnel
  set proposal aes256-sha256
  set dhgrp 14
  set auto-negotiate enable
 next
end
config firewall address
 edit Remote-LAN
  set subnet 198.51.100.0 255.255.255.0
 next
end
config firewall policy
 edit 100
  set srcintf port3
  set dstintf Site-B-Tunnel
  set srcaddr LAN-Subnet
  set dstaddr Remote-LAN
  set action accept
  set schedule always
  set service ALL
 next
end
config router static
 edit 10
  set dst 198.51.100.0 255.255.255.0
  set device Site-B-Tunnel
 next
end

key_parameters.description: Defines IKE phase 1 parameters and peer
Encryption and authentication algorithms for phase 1

concept_summary: FortiOS QoS shapes and prioritizes traffic using traffic shapers and policies. Traffic shaping controls bandwidth allocation per IP, per policy, or per application. Shapers define maximum and guaranteed bandwidth with priority levels. Application control identifies traffic by signature while traffic shaping enforces bandwidth limits. QoS integrates with security policies for unified traffic management.
cli_mode_context: Configure traffic shapers under 'config firewall shaper traffic-shaper'. Configure shaping policies under 'config firewall shaping-policy'. Apply shapers to firewall policies with traffic-shaping-policy parameter.
example_commands:
config firewall shaper traffic-shaper
 edit Voice-Shaper
  set maximum-bandwidth 2000
  set guaranteed-bandwidth 1000
  set priority high
 next
 edit Bulk-Shaper
  set maximum-bandwidth 5000
  set guaranteed-bandwidth 1000
  set priority low
 next
end
config firewall shaping-policy
 edit 1
  set name "Prioritize-Voice"
  set service VOIP
  set srcaddr all
  set dstaddr all
  set srcintf any
  set dstintf any
  set traffic-shaper Voice-Shaper
  set class-id 1
 next
end
config firewall policy
 edit 1
  set srcintf port3
  set dstintf port2
  set srcaddr all
  set dstaddr all
  set action accept
  set schedule always
  set service ALL
  set traffic-shaping-policy 1
 next
end

key_parameters.description: Applies shaping policy to firewall rule

concept_summary: FortiOS supports local and remote AAA using RADIUS, TACACS+, LDAP, or SAML for admin and user authentication. Admin authentication controls CLI/GUI access with privilege profiles. User authentication integrates with firewall policies for identity-based access control. Two-factor authentication adds security with FortiToken or third-party solutions. SSO enables transparent user identification.
cli_mode_context: Configure admin authentication under 'config system admin'. Configure user authentication servers under 'config user radius', 'config user tacacs+', or 'config user ldap'. Create user groups under 'config user group'. Reference auth in firewall policies.
example_commands:
config user radius
 edit RADIUS-Server
  set server 192.0.2.50
  set secret RadiusSecret123
  set auth-type auto
 next
end
config user group
 edit VPN-Users
  set member RADIUS-Server
 next
end
config system admin
 edit netadmin
  set remote-auth enable
  set accprofile prof_admin
  set vdom root
  set wildcard enable
  set remote-group VPN-Users
 next
end
config user tacacs+
 edit TACACS-Server
  set server 192.0.2.51
  set key TacacsSecret123
  set authen-type auto
 next
end

key_parameters.description: Creates user group with auth server members

concept_summary: FortiOS supports SNMP v1, v2c, and v3 for monitoring with OID support and trap generation. Logging sends events to local disk, memory, or remote syslog/FortiAnalyzer. Log levels and categories provide granular filtering. Security Fabric enables centralized monitoring across multiple FortiGates. FortiCloud and FortiAnalyzer offer cloud and on-premise log management solutions.
cli_mode_context: Configure SNMP under 'config system snmp sysinfo' and 'config system snmp community'. Configure logging under 'config log' with destinations including memory, disk, syslogd, or fortianalyzer.
example_commands:
config system snmp sysinfo
 set status enable
 set description "FG-HQ-FW01"
 set contact-info "netops@example.com"
 set location "DataCenter-01"
end
config system snmp community
 edit 1
  set name PublicRO
  set query-v1-status enable
  set query-v2c-status enable
  set hosts 192.0.2.100 255.255.255.255
 next
end
config log syslogd setting
 set status enable
 set server 192.0.2.200
 set port 514
 set facility local7
end
config log memory setting
 set status enable
end
config log fortianalyzer setting
 set status enable
 set server 192.0.2.150
 set reliable enable
end

key_parameters.description: Enables and configures SNMP system information
Defines SNMP community strings and access
Allowed NMS IP addresses for SNMP queries

concept_summary: FortiOS supports VXLAN for network virtualization in data center and SD-WAN deployments. VXLAN encapsulates Layer 2 frames in UDP for overlay networks. FortiGate can act as VXLAN VTEP for integrating physical and virtual networks. EVPN control plane support is available on select high-end FortiGate models for data center fabric integration.
cli_mode_context: Configure VXLAN under 'config system vxlan'. Set VNI, VTEP addresses, and associated interfaces. Support varies by platform model and may require specific licenses.
example_commands:
config system vxlan
 edit vxlan100
  set interface port2
  set vni 10100
  set remote-ip 203.0.113.10 203.0.113.20
 next
end
config system interface
 edit vxlan100
  set vdom root
  set type vxlan
 next
end
reason: VXLAN basic support exists but comprehensive EVPN-VXLAN with BGP control plane is limited to high-end FortiGate models and not widely documented for 7.4.x. FortiGate focus is security appliance rather than data center switching/EVPN fabric.

concept_summary: FortiOS has limited native MPLS support as it focuses on security appliance functionality rather than service provider routing. Some FortiGate models support basic MPLS forwarding for integration with MPLS networks. SD-WAN overlay provides alternative to traditional MPLS for WAN connectivity with application-aware routing and security.
cli_mode_context: MPLS configuration is platform-specific and limited. SD-WAN provides modern alternative with 'config system sdwan'.
example_commands:
config system sdwan
 set status enable
 config zone
  edit virtual-wan-link
  next
 end
 config members
  edit 1
   set interface port2
   set gateway 192.0.2.1
  next
  edit 2
   set interface port4
   set gateway 198.51.100.1
  next
 end
end

key_parameters.description: Configures SD-WAN as alternative to MPLS
Defines WAN interfaces participating in SD-WAN
Gateway IP for each WAN member

reason: Native MPLS L3VPN/L2VPN features are not core FortiGate capabilities. FortiGate focuses on security and SD-WAN rather than MPLS service provider functions. Basic MPLS passthrough may exist but not full PE router functionality.

concept_summary: FortiOS HA clustering provides device redundancy with active-passive or active-active operation. Configuration and session synchronization between cluster members ensures seamless failover. Heartbeat links monitor cluster health. HA supports configuration sync, session sync, and link monitoring for interface-level failover. Virtual clustering allows multiple virtual domains across cluster.
cli_mode_context: Configure HA under 'config system ha'. Set cluster mode, group name, password, heartbeat interfaces, and monitoring. Priority determines active unit. Override enables preemption.
example_commands:
config system ha
 set group-name FG-Production-HA
 set mode a-p
 set password ClusterSecret123
 set hbdev port7 50 port8 100
 set session-pickup enable
 set session-pickup-connectionless enable
 set ha-mgmt-status enable
 config ha-mgmt-interface
  edit 1
   set interface port1
   set gateway 192.0.2.1
  next
 end
 set priority 200
 set override enable
 set monitor port2 port3
end

key_parameters.description: Enables independent management access per unit
Enables preemption when higher priority unit recovers
Interfaces to monitor for failover triggering

concept_summary: FortiOS system management includes configuration backup and restore, firmware upgrades, disk management, and administrative access. Configuration can be backed up locally or to USB/TFTP/FTP. Firmware upgrades via GUI or CLI with automatic or manual reboot. FortiManager provides centralized management for multiple FortiGates. CLI and GUI share common configuration database enabling flexible management.
cli_mode_context: Use 'execute backup' commands for configuration backup. Use 'execute restore' for recovery. Use 'execute update-now' for firmware upgrade. Access configuration with 'show' commands.
example_commands:
execute backup config management-station 192.0.2.50 backup-config.conf
execute restore config management-station 192.0.2.50 restore-config.conf
execute backup full-config management-station 192.0.2.50 full-backup.tgz
show full-configuration
show system interface
execute update-now
execute reboot
execute factoryreset
diagnose sys top
get system status
get system performance status
execute disk list
execute date
execute time

key_parameters.description: Backs up configuration to file or remote server
Backs up config with encrypted passwords
